paragraphs: Children in care in South Lanarkshire are looked after by South Lanarkshire Council's own fostering service, based at the council offices in Hamilton, and by the independent agencies shown above. Its Family Connections team works with carers. During Foster Care Fortnight in May 2025 the council asked for more carers living in South Lanarkshire, and said it particularly needed people who could look after older children and brothers and sisters, so that families do not have to be split up.

The council describes two main kinds of fostering. Interim carers look after a child for days, weeks or months while plans are made for them to go home or move to a permanent family. Permanent carers give a long-term home to a child who cannot return to their birth family; the council says most of these children are over eight and some have brothers or sisters.

To apply you need to be over 21. You can live on your own, with a partner or with your family; couples need to have lived together for at least two years. You need a spare bedroom so that a child has a room of their own, and to be well enough to manage day-to-day care. The council says it welcomes carers from all backgrounds and will talk through things like pets and smoking with you.

Assessment includes home visits, checks and references, and the council aims to complete it within six months before your application goes to its fostering panel. Approved carers get a supervising social worker, regular training and support at any hour, along with a weekly allowance that depends on the child's age, a fee, and help with equipment and travel costs. The council runs information sessions with experienced foster carers in towns across the area; in June 2025 these included Larkhall, Stonehouse, Carluke, New Lanark and Calderglen.
Before you decide, speak to the council and to two or three of the agencies above, and ask each what training, support and payments they offer for the children you could care for.
